title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
authors: Vipin Kurian Elavunkel, Sylvain Le Tonquesse, Hadrien Vroylandt
abstract: Identifying earth-abundant catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a central challenge in scalable green hydrogen production. We present a computational pipeline that couples diffusion-based generative modelling, machine-learning force-field relaxation, and graph neural network (GNN) property prediction to discover bimetallic HER catalysts beyond the structures and stoichiometries covered by existing adsorption databases. A generative model (MatterGen) is fine-tuned on bulk alloy structures labelled with their minimum hydrogen adsorption energy and steered towards adsorption energies near zero. From the generated pool we retain the stable structures that are novel bimetallic alloys: binary compositions built from the training-set metals but at stoichiometries or structures absent from that database. Each candidate's low-index facets are ranked by a machine-learning-force-field (MatterSim) surface-energy screen, and only the most stable terminations are converted into explicit slab models with hydrogen adsorbed at all high-symmetry surface sites and relaxed with the same force field. Two GNN surrogates (MEGNet and ALIGNN), trained on a high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) dataset, then screen the resulting slab candidates. Because the two models encode the local environment through different inductive biases, we retain only the alloys on which both agree, reducing the influence of any single model. This consensus screening, combined with a MatterSim energy-difference triangulation, resulted in a shortlist of near-thermoneutral bimetallic candidates. Eight are validated with plane-wave DFT, and four of them, Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3, bind hydrogen within the thermoneutral window. All eight alloys are dynamically stable by phonon calculations. These four alloys are highlighted as DFT-validated bimetallic HER candidates for experimental follow-up.

infographic.key_insight: An AI-guided discovery pipeline identified four novel bimetallic alloys with DFT-validated, near-thermoneutral hydrogen binding as promising hydrogen evolution reaction catalysts.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Generative design and consensus screening can prioritize alloy compositions beyond existing databases, focusing costly DFT calculations and experimental follow-up.
method: Fine-tune MatterGen on adsorption-labelled bulk alloys to generate novel binary structures targeting near-zero hydrogen adsorption energy.
Use MatterSim to assess stability, rank low-index facets, and relax hydrogen-covered slabs.
Combine MEGNet–ALIGNN agreement with MatterSim energy-difference checks to shortlist candidates for DFT validation.
infographic.evidence_signal: Of eight DFT-tested alloys, Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3 showed hydrogen binding within the thermoneutral window; all eight were dynamically stable in phonon calculations.
infographic.watch_item: Near-thermoneutral binding and phonon stability do not establish experimental HER activity, operating durability, or affordability; the four highlighted alloys all contain precious metals.
infographic.paper_title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction

title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
authors: Xuwei Liu, Zhimin Zhang, Xiaoguang Hu, Zhongwei Liu, Yuanhui Sun, Jun Huo
abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

infographic.key_insight: PaddleMaterials unifies six materials-learning task classes with verifiable cross-task interfaces and optional compiled execution.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Engineers can connect materials design, simulation and characterization models while preserving physical quantities, units and reference conventions.
method: Standardize data processing, training, evaluation and pretrained-model management across six task classes.
Record scientific semantics in task interfaces to verify cross-task composition.
Enable graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted compilation without changing model definitions.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compilation accelerated every instance in eight groups; LiMnO2 formation-energy predictions differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV/atom, with model-step costs below one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation.
infographic.watch_item: Compilation did not accelerate every instance across all groups, and the case studies do not establish accuracy across broader materials and chemistries.
infographic.paper_title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science

title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
authors: Junchi Liu, Haoran Si, Luo Yan, Sergei Tretiak, Liujiang Zhou
abstract: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37\%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86\% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15\% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.

infographic.key_insight: ST2M uses crystallographic symmetry to generate crystal candidates, achieving 96.37% structural validity while improving the joint rate of stability, uniqueness, and novelty.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Generating candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints could streamline computational materials screening and discovery.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Use Wyckoff-pattern conditioning and degree-of-freedom masks to constrain generation.
Jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables with a twin-branch Transformer.
infographic.evidence_signal: For known dataset patterns, 23.86% of generated structures met stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria—a 68.15% relative improvement over the best baseline; first-principles calculations identified 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
infographic.watch_item: First-principles validation covered selected candidates, so it does not establish the stability rate across all generated structures.
infographic.paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation

title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
authors: Hrishi V. Harsora, Ashutosh Krishna Amaram, Raghavan Ranganathan, Tarun K. Agarwal
abstract: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.

infographic.key_insight: A closed-loop search calibrates atomistic GaAs growth kinetics directly from experimental growth data, reducing reliance on costly DFT-derived rate parameters.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework turns routine MOCVD growth measurements into a mechanistically interpretable model that could support process optimization.
method: Simulate atomistic deposition events with kinetic Monte Carlo.
Use Monte Carlo Tree Search to calibrate kinetic rate parameters against experimental growth data.
Steer the search using each parameter’s degree of rate control.
infographic.evidence_signal: For GaAs MOCVD, the calibrated model captures the measured temperature dependence of growth rate and recovers three known kinetic regimes with changing rate-determining steps.
infographic.watch_item: Calibration depends on the chosen reaction-event model, and the abstract does not report quantitative errors or validation beyond GaAs.
infographic.paper_title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations

title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
authors: Eric A. Lass, Carla Joyce C. Nocheseda, Christopher Tandoc, Yong-Jie Hu, Peter K. Liaw
abstract: Refractory compositionally complex alloys (R-CCAs) show great promise as next generation structural materials for extreme conditions, but alloys with excellent high temperature mechanical properties most often exhibit virtually zero room temperature tensile ductility, hindering potential commercial application. Several semi-empirical metrics have been employed for predicting plasticity in R-CCAs, including valence electron concentration, Pugh ratio, Rice criteria, and the D-parameter. While many currently available ductility metrics correlate very well when compressive plasticity is considered, only the density functional theory (DFT) based D-parameter shows a strong correlation in tension. A new ductility metric is developed using CALculation of PHAse Diagrams (CALPHAD) thermodynamics, Gamma, with includes the free energy difference between the body-centered cubic (BCC) and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phases, the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface, and an electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion. The Gamma parameter exhibits better correlation with tensile ductility than D-parameter and performs equally well in compression. While this improvement is modest, a thermodynamically grounded ductility metric is clearly required to capture intrinsic ductility behavior. Extrinsic contributions to brittle behavior in R-CCAs, namely interstitial oxygen content, are also briefly discussed. Combining the Gamma ductility parameter with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility is proposed as a first order attempt to capture both intrinsic and extrinsic contributions to ductile behavior in R-CCAs.

infographic.key_insight: A CALPHAD-based Γ ductility metric modestly improves prediction of room-temperature tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys over the DFT-based D-parameter.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The metric could help screen refractory alloys for intrinsic ductility while preserving their potential for high-temperature structural applications.
method: Combine the BCC–HCP free-energy difference with the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface.
Include an electronegativity-corrected lattice-distortion contribution.
Propose pairing Γ with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility to account for extrinsic embrittlement.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports better correlation with tensile ductility than the D-parameter and comparable performance in compression, but provides no numerical evaluation results.
infographic.watch_item: The improvement is modest, and combining Γ with oxygen solubility remains a proposed first-order approach rather than a demonstrated comprehensive predictor.
infographic.paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys

title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
authors: Adam M. Krajewski, Ricardo Amaral, Jonathan W. Siegel, Luke A. Myers, Rushi Gong, Shun-Li Shang
abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

infographic.key_insight: crystALL generates structurally diverse candidate ensembles beyond the convex hull, prioritizing stable and metastable configurations rather than ground-state stability alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Including metastable structures can help engineers interpret experimental materials and investigate properties missed by stability-only searches.
method: Generate candidates through species substitutions using a large relaxed-structure pool.
Analyze candidates in pySIPFENN ML feature space, then select representatives by clustering and energy minimization or property matching.
Build ensembles for validation, searching anonymized compositional ranges when experimental stoichiometry is uncertain.
infographic.evidence_signal: The approach draws on 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD; the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or runtime benchmarks.
infographic.watch_item: Candidate diversity alone does not establish thermodynamic populations or experimental accessibility; experimental or ab initio validation remains necessary.
infographic.paper_title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach

title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
authors: Chengji Li, Fan Zheng
abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories. The method combines explicit external-field coupling with self-consistent updates of electronic density while retaining the computational efficiency of the classical-path approximation. Benchmarks against regular TDDFT methods show close agreement for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses. Applications to the linear absorption spectrum of crystalline and amorphous SiO$_2$ demonstrate its capability to large and structurally complex systems. This method is also applied to the 2D hybrid perovskite $(\mathrm{BA})_2\mathrm{CsPb}_2\mathrm{Br}_7$. Finite-temperature calculations show that the second-order opto-current response is strongly affected by structural fluctuations. Real-space DC current density further reveals pronounced Br-centered vortex currents, and its microscopic origin is investigated.

infographic.key_insight: CPA-NAMD-extF extends classical-path nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to field-driven electronic responses, revealing fluctuation-sensitive opto-currents and Br-centered vortex currents in a 2D hybrid perovskite.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient finite-temperature modeling of optical and electronic responses in large, structurally complex materials.
method: Propagate a first-principles electronic density matrix along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
Include explicit external-field coupling and self-consistent electronic-density updates.
Apply the framework to crystalline and amorphous SiO₂ and (BA)₂CsPb₂Br₇.
infographic.evidence_signal: Benchmarks show close agreement with regular TDDFT for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses; perovskite calculations reveal strong structural-fluctuation effects on second-order opto-current.
infographic.watch_item: Precomputed ionic trajectories retain the classical-path approximation, so field-induced feedback on ionic motion requires careful assessment.
infographic.paper_title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field

title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
authors: Suhas Suresh Bharadwaj
abstract: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

infographic.key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints recovers the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields without destructive testing.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could enable non-destructive characterization of shear electromechanical coupling relevant to PMUT and surface acoustic wave devices.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers in network outputs to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train using coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and observation misfit, eliminating boundary and initial-condition penalty weights.
Non-dimensionalize governing coefficients to improve numerical balance.
infographic.evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
infographic.watch_item: Validation uses simulated plane-strain data; performance on physical devices with uncertain geometry, boundary conditions, or material models remains unverified.
infographic.paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints

title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
authors: Luqing Wang, Qunfei Zhou, Qiucheng Li, Venkata Surya Chaitanya Kolluru, Hui Li, Albert Tsui
abstract: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML). Importantly, incorporating ML-predicted charge transfer as an input feature to a subsequent ML model enables physics-informed predictions of binding energies. Additional DFT calculations on four representative cases were performed to validate the ML predictions. SHAP analysis reveals that the majority of key descriptors are associated with delocalized electrons, highlighting the role of electronic properties in governing binding strength. Combined DFT and ML screening identifies 65 and 73 promising boride surfaces for the v1/6 and v1/9 phases, respectively. Al- and Ag-based borides, including AlB2 and AgB2, emerge as predominant candidates for both phases. The computationally predicted candidate substrates and the deduced design guidelines provide a charge-transfer-informed ML strategy for substrate selection and represent promising steps toward the experimental realization of freestanding borophene.

infographic.key_insight: Charge-transfer-informed machine learning identifies promising boride substrates with tunable borophene binding, with Al- and Ag-based borides emerging as leading candidates.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Better substrate selection could ease borophene release and support its integration into quantum and energy technologies.
method: Combine DFT and ML to screen 1,356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases, ν1/6 and ν1/9.
Use ML-predicted charge transfer as an input to binding-energy prediction.
Apply SHAP analysis to identify influential descriptors, highlighting delocalized-electron properties.
infographic.evidence_signal: The screening identified 65 promising surfaces for ν1/6 and 73 for ν1/9, with additional DFT calculations on four representative cases used to validate ML predictions.
infographic.watch_item: The candidates remain computational predictions; experimental synthesis and successful borophene release are not demonstrated in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis

title: Learning from high-resolution 2D images to reconstruct 3D microstructures
authors: Wenbo Sui, Lars P. Mikkelsen, Jens W. Andreasen, Daniel Lichau, Harold Phelippeau, Philip J. Withers
abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) microstructure characterization remains difficult to undertake at scale because volumetric imaging at the required spatial resolution is expensive, time-consuming or destructive. In many settings, however, fine-resolution two-dimensional (2D) imaging and lower-resolution volumetric measurements are both readily available. We introduce a Privileged Cross-modal Relational Distillation (PCRD) framework that leverages fine-resolution 2D observations during training to improve specimen-specific 3D reconstruction from lower-resolution volumetric imaging alone. We demonstrate PCRD on pultruded carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites, using scanning electron microscopy as the privileged modality and micro-CT as the inference input. The framework transfers spatial organization by matching similarity distributions defined around corresponding spatial anchors in the teacher and student representations, avoiding direct alignment of heterogeneous feature vectors. In 2D cross-sectional reconstruction, PCRD improves mAP by 1.66 percentage points over direct micro-CT training. Independent 3D validation against high-resolution synchrotron X-ray CT data shows close agreement in fiber volume fraction, diameter and local spacing. The PCRD reconstruction matches 89.97% of the reference fiber centerline length, compared with 75.08% for the interpolated low-resolution volume.

infographic.key_insight: Privileged Cross-modal Relational Distillation (PCRD) uses high-resolution 2D images during training to improve specimen-specific 3D microstructure reconstruction from lower-resolution volumetric images alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly high-resolution 3D imaging when characterizing carbon fiber-reinforced polymer microstructures.
method: Use scanning electron microscopy as the privileged training modality and micro-CT as the inference input.
Transfer spatial organization by matching similarity distributions around corresponding spatial anchors.
Distill relational information without directly aligning heterogeneous feature vectors.
infographic.evidence_signal: PCRD improved 2D reconstruction mAP by 1.66 percentage points over direct micro-CT training and matched 89.97% of reference fiber centerline length in independent synchrotron CT validation, versus 75.08% for the interpolated low-resolution volume.
infographic.watch_item: Training requires corresponding spatial anchors across modalities; robustness to imperfect correspondence and generalization beyond the demonstrated composite remain to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Learning from high-resolution 2D images to reconstruct 3D microstructures

title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
authors: Min-Ju Choi, Le Wang, Krishna Prasad Koirala, Hyoju Park, Mark E. Bowden, Elizabeth Helen Krenkel
abstract: Rare-earth nickelates are among the most active oxide electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), owing to their tunable Ni-O covalency, near-unity eg occupancy, and sensitivity to A-site chemistry, oxygen stoichiometry, and epitaxial strain. Here, we use epitaxial A-site high-entropy (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 thin films to reveal how epitaxial strain influences defect formation, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER activity in a chemically disordered rare-earth (RE) sublattice. Tensile strain promotes Ruddlesden-Popper fault formation, interrupts the corner-sharing NiO6 network, and lowers the average Ni oxidation state. Although the occupied density of states near the Fermi level remains largely unchanged, O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals increased low-energy unoccupied states under tensile strain. First-principles calculations suggest that tensile strain shifts RE 4f-derived states toward the Fermi level, enhancing RE 4f-O 2p-Ni 3d hybridization. These coupled structural and electronic changes lead to earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates. The high-entropy nickelate also shows enhanced resistance to OER-induced structural degradation compared with LaNiO3. These results suggest that A-site configurational disorder and epitaxial strain can jointly tune defect formation and rare-earth-derived electronic states, providing a route for improving perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.

infographic.key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly tune nickelate defects and electronic states, improving oxygen evolution activity while the high-entropy material resists degradation better than LaNiO3.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Combining rare-earth mixing with epitaxial strain offers a route to more active and durable perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.
method: Studied epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probed structural defects, Ni valence, electronic states, and OER performance.
Used first-principles calculations to investigate strain-dependent rare-earth orbital hybridization.
infographic.evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films showed earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy material also resisted structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability benchmarks, and transfer from epitaxial films to scalable electrodes remains unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films

title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
authors: Vsevolod Biryukov, Sergey V. Barabash, Pranab Kumar Das, Jack Deslippe, Mauro Del Ben, Felipe H. da Jornada
abstract: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.

infographic.key_insight: Quantum 3xplorer shows how scientist-supervised AI coding agents can build a quantum simulation engine in weeks, with plane-wave DFT as its first validation case.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Its layered architecture, schema-validated inputs and outputs, and GPU-supercomputer scaling offer a foundation for extensible, AI-ready materials modeling workflows.
method: Domain scientists define physics and validation criteria; AI agents write, test, and optimize code.
Implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT with multiple formalisms, forces, stresses, and structural relaxation.
Separate abstract quantum concepts from numerical representations to support future extensions.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with established reference implementations, faster single-core execution in representative benchmarks, and scaling across GPU-accelerated supercomputers, without quantitative details.
infographic.watch_item: Validation beyond plane-wave DFT and the generality of reported performance gains remain to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling

title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
authors: Arda Uzunoglu, Mahler Revsine, Michael Schatz, Benjamin Van Durme, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Daniel Khashabi
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

infographic.key_insight: Facts seen only once during training—called monofacts—are identified as a key factor governing LLM scientific discovery capacity.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For materials-discovery models, training-data design should consider monofact rates alongside dataset size and diversity.
method: Model discovery capacity through a missing-probability-mass framework.
Directly vary monofact rates in materials-science and regulatory-genomics training sets.
Test discovery outcomes across model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets.
infographic.evidence_signal: Higher monofact rates consistently yielded more discoveries across two open-weight model families, with additional experiments indicating the effect was not explained by training-set diversity alone.
infographic.watch_item: Cross-domain transfer was observed when paired with in-domain data; the abstract does not establish generalization to arbitrary scientific domains.
infographic.paper_title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data

title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
authors: Auronno Ovid Hussain, Adith Saha Dipro, Muhammad Anisuzzaman Talukder
abstract: Water electrolysis is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen (H$_2$) production. However, gas bubble formation significantly degrades the electrochemical surface area ($A_{\rm EC}$) and the electrocatalytic activity of microstructured electrodes in water electrolyzer cells. Existing theoretical models fail to connect computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and electrochemistry to analyze how bubble dynamics affect the performance of gas-evolving microstructured electrodes. This work develops a multiphysics-based theoretical model that couples two-phase CFD with Butler-Volmer and Faradaic kinetics, incorporating exchange current density, cell current, gravitational acceleration, surface tension, and fluid properties such as density and viscosity. The model quantifies essential electrochemical parameters, such as the enhancement in $A_{\rm EC}$ and the overpotential ($η$), which deviate by less than 7\% and 15\%, respectively, from the experimental results. Evaluations of the fabricated microstructured electrodes using polarization curves, cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and linear polarization resistance techniques demonstrate reduced $η$ by 2.49--21.39\% and 9.55--24.32\% for oxygen (O$_2$) and H$_2$ evolution, respectively. Furthermore, the model reveals the interplay between enhanced geometric surface area and bubble-transport limitations, facilitating the optimization and analysis of structural parameters. These findings establish a physics-informed roadmap for designing optimal, robust, and industry-scalable microstructured electrodes for efficient H$_2$ generation via water electrolysis.

infographic.key_insight: Microstructured copper electrodes can reduce electrolysis overpotential, but their added surface area must be balanced against bubble-induced blockage and transport losses.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Coupled bubble-flow and electrochemical modeling can guide electrode geometry design for more efficient alkaline hydrogen production.
method: Couple two-phase CFD with Butler–Volmer and Faradaic kinetics.
Model bubble effects on electrochemical surface area and overpotential.
Validate fabricated electrodes using polarization curves, cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy, and linear polarization resistance.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports model deviations below 7% for electrochemical surface-area enhancement and 15% for overpotential, with experimental overpotential reductions of 2.49–21.39% for oxygen evolution and 9.55–24.32% for hydrogen evolution.
infographic.watch_item: Industrial scalability is proposed, but the abstract does not establish long-term durability or performance under industrial operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
authors: Sunraj Patel, Krishanu Biswas
abstract: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX$_3$ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX$_3$ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2\%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3\%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

infographic.key_insight: Diffusion generation expands ABX₃ perovskite composition and ordering diversity, but does not establish enrichment near the 1.4 eV bandgap target.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Generated structures offer candidates beyond a two-prototype substitution reference, provided topology, relaxation stability and property predictions are independently checked.
method: Generate candidate ABX₃ structures with a pretrained diffusion model.
Filter for three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskite connectivity.
Assess chemistry and ALIGNN-predicted bandgaps; check six structures with first-principles calculations.
infographic.evidence_signal: The target-window fraction was 8.2% for generated structures versus 7.3% for the Materials Project reference; ALIGNN performed well on a formula-grouped random split but failed to outperform a constant baseline on a severe B-site-disjoint test.
infographic.watch_item: Different MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources limit target-enrichment claims, while relaxation can change structural classification and calculated gaps can differ appreciably from predictions.
infographic.paper_title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery

title: ElectroChemLLM: A Multimodal LLM Pipeline for High-Fidelity Electrochemical Informatics
authors: Dikshya Mohanty, Manoj Praveen Nandigama, Kuldeepsinh Raj, Sourav Kanti Maiti, Jiannan Yang, Ruiqi Luo
abstract: Electrochemistry is central to solving many modern-day challenges, including energy storage systems for a sustainable future, and its advancement relies heavily on the data from past findings. Existing automated pipelines are limited by text-only architectures, context fragmentation, and numerical hallucinations - collectively preventing accurate, large-scale curation of property databases. We introduce ElectrochemLLM, a multimodal information extraction pipeline that jointly identifies structured electrochemical records encompassing electrolyte compositions, electrode materials, cell configurations, and their measured physicochemical properties from unstructured scientific PDFs at scale. By combining hybrid document parsing with vision-capable LLM orchestration, the pipeline extracts verifiable, structured data across text, tables, and figures. Evaluated on the battery-electrolyte subset of our manually annotated benchmark of 232 papers, ElectrochemLLM achieves an F-1 score of 0.97, and has been applied to curate ElectroChemDB, a structured database spanning 15,000 electrochemical research articles. We demonstrate the utility of this resource by training machine learning models for electrolyte property prediction, illustrating a complete pathway from unstructured literature to predictive materials discovery.

infographic.key_insight: ElectrochemLLM converts scientific PDFs into structured electrochemical records, linking literature extraction to electrolyte property prediction.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The pipeline can support materials screening by organizing electrolyte compositions, electrode materials, cell configurations, and measured properties into reusable datasets.
method: Combine hybrid document parsing with vision-capable LLM orchestration.
Extract verifiable records across text, tables, and figures.
Train electrolyte property prediction models using the curated ElectroChemDB.
infographic.evidence_signal: The pipeline reports an F1 score of 0.97 on the battery-electrolyte subset of a manually annotated 232-paper benchmark and was applied to 15,000 electrochemical research articles.
infographic.watch_item: The reported F1 applies to a benchmark subset; extraction accuracy across other electrochemical domains and downstream prediction performance require further validation.
infographic.paper_title: ElectroChemLLM: A Multimodal LLM Pipeline for High-Fidelity Electrochemical Informatics

title: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?
authors: Mohammed Al-Fahdi, Aakash Naik, Katharina Ueltzen, Luc Walterbos, Tom Demeyere, Philipp Benner
abstract: Chemical bonding is the language through which chemistry rationalizes materials structure, stability, properties, and reactivity. Meanwhile, modern deep-learning models achieve remarkable predictive performance using representations based largely on compositional and structural information, raising the question of whether explicit bonding concepts remain necessary. In this work, we argue that artificial intelligence does not render chemical bonding obsolete but provides a new framework for evaluating and refining bonding concepts. We show that, through linear probing, Allegro and MACE embeddings recover bonding descriptors with (R^2 > 0.95), indicating that bonding emerges naturally from Allegro's and MACE's latent spaces. We also show that bonding descriptors provide information beyond bond distance in our electronic-structure-featurized MEGNet (ESF-MEGNet) model, reducing prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%. We discuss implications for interpretable machine learning, synthesizability prediction, and generative materials design, and suggest joint-embedding approaches for learning more general bonding representations. More broadly, we propose that chemical bonding can be understood as a learnable representation of electronic structure. From this perspective, different bonding models represent alternative compressions of the underlying electronic information and can be evaluated through their predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity. The age of machine learning shifts the focus from whether a bonding model is physically motivated to whether it captures the information required to explain and predict materials behavior. If a materials genome exists, it should be encodable through a representation of chemical bonding. If no bonding representation can capture this information, our understanding of the chemical bond may require revision.

infographic.key_insight: Chemical bonding remains useful in AI-driven materials science as a learnable representation of electronic structure that can emerge within neural-network embeddings.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Explicit bonding descriptors can improve mechanical-property predictions and support more interpretable models for materials discovery.
method: Linearly probe Allegro and MACE embeddings for bonding descriptors.
Add electronic-structure-based bonding features to ESF-MEGNet.
Frame bonding models as compressed electronic information, evaluated by predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity.
infographic.evidence_signal: Linear probes recover bonding descriptors with R² > 0.95, while ESF-MEGNet bonding features add information beyond bond distance and reduce prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset coverage or evaluation splits, leaving generalization to unfamiliar materials uncertain.
infographic.paper_title: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?

title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
authors: Tomke E. Glier, Nicholas J. Weadock, Julian A. Vigil, Cole Shank, Xixi Qin, Gabriel J. Graf
abstract: Understanding and controlling the optical, thermal and mechanical properties of K$_2$PtCl$_6$-type double perovskites is essential for the design of lead-free, high-performance thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials. In this study, we investigate Cs$_2$SnI$_6$ using temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman scattering, complemented by density functional theory-based phonon calculations. The appearance of Raman-forbidden phonon modes in the Raman response at cryogenic temperatures provides strong evidence for local symmetry breaking that does not develop into a global structural phase transition. Through detailed analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes, we characterize the temperature evolution of the symmetry-broken structural response of Cs$_2$SnI$_6$. Below 200 K, multi-phonon scattering is strongly enhanced, and symmetry-forbidden Raman modes emerge. The temperature dependence of phonon intensities follows a phenomenological Arrhenius behavior, revealing an activation energy of 15-20 meV. These results establish temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of local structural distortions and anharmonic structural dynamics in Cs$_2$SnI$_6$, providing a robust experimental basis for discussing the microscopic origins of symmetry breaking and electron-phonon coupling in halide double perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: Cryogenic Raman signatures reveal local symmetry breaking in Cs₂SnI₆ without a global structural phase transition.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding local distortions and anharmonic dynamics could inform the design of lead-free thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials.
method: Temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman spectroscopy
Density functional theory-based phonon calculations
Analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes
infographic.evidence_signal: Below 200 K, enhanced multi-phonon scattering and Raman-forbidden modes emerge, while phonon intensity trends yield a phenomenological Arrhenius activation energy of 15–20 meV.
infographic.watch_item: The Raman evidence supports local symmetry breaking but does not uniquely establish its microscopic origin or demonstrate improved device performance.
infographic.paper_title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$

title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,532 articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their steady-state reference efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.key_insight: Training language models on structured experimental evidence improved perovskite reasoning and guided a contact-material choice that outperformed the expert-preferred alternative.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could help engineers connect experimental controls, observations and mechanisms to better perovskite solar-cell designs.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,532 articles.
Adapt OpenPerov using linked strategies, controls, observations and mechanistic interpretations.
Evaluate scientific reasoning and experimentally test an AI-selected self-assembled monolayer contact.
infographic.evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash led 13 closed-book systems; the selected contact enabled 27.05% efficiency and 96.74% retention of steady-state reference efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 °C.
infographic.watch_item: The reported material-design test is narrow, and dark thermal ageing does not establish durability under illuminated operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization

title: On-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
authors: Sayan Bhowmik, John E. Pask, Phanish Suryanarayana
abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force field ($Δ$-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that $Δ$-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm$^3$ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.

infographic.key_insight: An on-the-fly Δ-machine learned force field combines a Yukawa reference model with learned DFT corrections to simulate warm dense matter accurately at up to 1,000× the speed of ab initio molecular dynamics.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient prediction of equation-of-state, structural, and transport properties of warm dense magnesium under extreme conditions.
method: Fit a Yukawa model on the fly to capture dominant screened-Coulomb ion interactions.
Use kernel learning and Bayesian linear regression to learn energy, force, and stress corrections relative to Kohn–Sham DFT.
Apply the corrected force field in molecular dynamics simulations.
infographic.evidence_signal: Validation against published warm dense carbon DFT results showed lower errors than standard MLFF at comparable cost; magnesium simulations covered 5.22–10.44 g/cm³ and 600 kK–1.5 MK.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy outside the studied materials and conditions remains to be established, and on-the-fly fitting still requires DFT reference calculations.
infographic.paper_title: On-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
